Title: instance of
Description:
instance of: that class of which this subject is a particular example and member; different from P279 (subclass of); for example: K2 is an instance of mountain; volcano is a subclass of mountain (and an instance of volcanic landform)
Wikibase value:film (Q11424)
short film (Q24862)
television film (Q506240)
anthology film (Q336144)
Examples: 12 Angry Men <instance of> film

Title: title
Description:
original title and title: published name of a work, such as a newspaper article, a literary work, piece of music, a website, or a performance work
language = original language
Wikidata qualifier: ISO 9:1995 (P2183), transliteration (P2440)
Examples: 12 Angry Men <title> 12 Angry Men (English)

Title: publication date
Description:
publication date: date or point in time when a work was first published or released
Wikidata qualifier: place of publication (P291) (country, film festival, geographic region). List each place in a separate statement
Examples: 12 Angry Men <publication date> 1957

Title: original language of film or TV show
Description:
original language: language in which a film or a performance work was originally created. Deprecated for written works and songs; use P407 ("language of work or name") instead.
• silent film → N/A (Q21686005)
Examples: 12 Angry Men <original language of film or TV show> English

Title: genre
Description: genre and by genre: creative work's genre or an artist's field of work (P101). Use main subject (P921) to relate creative works to their topic
Examples: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial <genre> science fiction film

Title: director
Description: director, theatrical director, film director, film or television director, television director and radio director: director(s) of film, TV-series, stageplay, video game or similar
Examples: 12 Angry Men <director> Sidney Lumet

Title: cast member
Description:
actor, film actor, television actor, singer, ballet dancer, stage actor, animal actor, performing artist, seiyū, cast member, pornographic actor, radio actor, model, musical theatre actor, actress, reality television participant, cast member of, opera singer, drag queen and kabuki actor: actor in the subject production [use "character role" (P453) and/or "name of the character role" (P4633) as qualifiers] [use "voice actor" (P725) for voice-only role]
Wikidata qualifier: character role (P453), subject named as (P1810)
Examples: 12 Angry Men <cast member> Martin Balsam

Title: director of photography
Description: cinematographer: person responsible for the framing, lighting, and filtration of the subject work
Examples: 12 Angry Men <director of photography> Boris Kaufman

Title: screenwriter
Description: screenwriter and film screenwriter: person(s) who wrote the script for subject item
Examples: 12 Angry Men <screenwriter> Reginald Rose

Title: film editor
Description: film editor: person who works with the raw footage, selecting shots and combining them into sequences to create a finished motion picture
Examples: 12 Angry Men <film editor> Carl Lerner

Title: producer
Description: producer: person(s) who produced the film, musical work, theatrical production, etc. (for film, this does not include executive producers, associate producers, etc.) [for production company, use P272, video games - use P178]
Examples: 12 Angry Men <producer> Henry Fonda

Title: narrative location
Description: narrative location: the narrative of the work is set in this location
Examples: 12 Angry Men <narrative location> New York City

Title: filming location
Description: filming location and filmed here: actual place where this scene/film was shot. For the setting, use "narrative location" (P840)
Examples: Lucy <filming location> Cité du Cinéma

Title: country of origin
Description: country of origin: country of origin of this item (creative work, food, phrase, product, etc.)
Examples: 12 Angry Men <country of origin> United States of America

Title: image
Description: illustration and image: image of relevant illustration of the subject; if available, also use more specific properties (sample: coat of arms image, locator map, flag image, signature image, logo image, collage image)
Examples: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea <image> 20,000 Leagues under the Sea - movie scene - newspaper July 1917.jpg

Title: film poster
Description: film poster: poster used to promote and advertise this film (if file is available on Commons). Use P154 for logos, P18 for movie stills and related images. Items about film posters can be linked with the qualifier "subject of" (P805).
Examples: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea <film poster> Poster - 20,000 Leagues under the Sea (1916).jpg

Title: video
Description: video recording: relevant video. For images, use the property P18. For film trailers, qualify with "object has role" (P3831)="trailer" (Q622550)
Examples: The Birds <video> The Birds trailer (1963).webm

Title: executive producer
Description: executive producer: executive producer of a movie or TV show
Examples: Lucy <executive producer> Marc Shmuger

Title: production company
Description: production company: company that produced this film, audio or performing arts work
Examples: The Scarlet Runner <production company> Vitagraph Studios

Title: composer
Description: composer: person(s) who wrote the music [for lyricist, use "lyrics by" (P676)]
Examples: The Internet's Own Boy: The Story of Aaron Swartz <composer> John Dragonetti

Title: voice actor
Description: voice actor: performer of a spoken role in a creative work such as animation, video game, radio drama, or dubbing over [use "character role" (P453) as qualifier] [use "cast member" (P161) for live acting]
Examples: Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope <voice actor> James Earl Jones

Title: based on
Description: based on: the work(s) used as the basis for subject item
Examples: 12 Angry Men <based on> Twelve Angry Men

Title: after a work by
Description: creative work: artist whose work strongly inspired/ was copied in this item
Examples: Here There Be Tygers <after a work by> Ray Bradbury

Title: main subject
Description: topic, matter, topic of a work and subject: primary topic of a work (see also P180: depicts)
Examples: 12 Angry Men <main subject> jury

Title: set in period
Description: historical period: historical, contemporary, or future period, year, century or day the work or genre is set in or event featured in the story of the work
Examples: Mary Poppins <set in period> Edwardian era

Title: list of characters
Description: Wikimedia list of fictional characters: Wikimedia page with the list of characters for this work
Examples: 12 Angry Men <list of characters> jury

Title: soundtrack release
Description: soundtrack album, soundtrack single and soundtrack extended play: music release that incorporates music directly recorded from the soundtrack of an audiovisual work
Examples: Skyfall <soundtrack release> Skyfall – Original Motion Picture Soundtrack

Title: color
Description:
color: color of subject
Wikibase value=black and white (Q838368), color (Q22006653)
Examples: Metropolis <color> black and white

Title: aspect ratio (W:H)
Description: aspect ratio: image width to height ratio of films, photographs, and other images
Examples: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial <aspect ratio (W:H)> 1.85:1

Title: average shot length
Description: average shot length: cinemetrical measure
Examples: The Bourne Supremacy <average shot length> 2.4 seconds

Title: significant event
Examples: Spectre <significant event> principal photography

Title: part of the series
Description:
series, series of creative works, event sequence, book series and painting series: series which contains the subject
Wikidata qualifier: follows (P155), followed by (P156), series ordinal (P1545)
Examples: The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe <part of the series> The Chronicles of Narnia

Title: different from
Description:
difference and different from: item that is different from another item, with which it may be confused
For multiple-language version film (Q2518205): Wikidata qualifier: criterion used (P1013)= multiple-language version film (Q2518205)
Examples: A Woman Who Knows What She Wants <different from> A Woman Who Knows What She Wants

Title: has quality
Description:
quality: the entity has an inherent or distinguishing non-material characteristic
Wikidata qualifier: title (P1476)
Examples: Naked Gun 33⅓: The Final Insult <has quality> title for Quebec

Title: working title
Description: working title: temporary name of a product or project used during its development
Examples: Bridge of Spies <working title> St. James Place

Title: cost
Description: cost: amount of money spent on building or producing an object
Examples: Creasyville Covered Bridge <cost> 301.25 United States dollar

Title: box office
Description: box office: box office takings accumulated by a film
Examples: Skyfall <box office> 1,108,561,013 United States dollar

Title: narrator
Description: storyteller and narrator: narrator, character or person that tells the story
Examples: Titanic <narrator> Gloria Stuart

Title: costume designer
Description: costume designer: person who designed the costumes for a film, television programme, etc
Examples: The Revenant <costume designer> Jacqueline West

Title: production designer
Description: production designer: person(s) responsible for overall aesthetic of the story of this motion picture, play, video game or similar; responsible for visual concept, producing interior, exterior, location, graphics, etc; deals with many and varied logistic related to this
Examples: Gone with the Wind <production designer> William Cameron Menzies

Title: duration
Description: duration: length of time of an event or process
Examples: La Grande Vadrouille <duration> 132 minute

Title: distributed by
Description: distributor: distributor of a creative work; distributor for a record label; news agency; film distributor
Examples: Rush Hour <distributed by> New Line Cinema

Title: copyright status
Description: copyright status: copyright status for intellectual creations like works of art, publications, software, etc.
Examples: Parasite <copyright status> copyrighted

Title: sound designer
Description: sound designer: person responsible for the sound on a stage, in a film or in a radio drama
Examples: Son of Saul <sound designer> Tamás Zányi

Title: presented in
Description: event at which a talk, film, paper, or poster was presented
Examples: The Shape of Water <presented in> 2017 Toronto International Film Festival

Title: award received
Description: award, honorary citizenship and title of honor: award or recognition received by a person, organization or creative work
Examples: 12 Angry Men <award received> Golden Bear

Title: review score
Description: value judgment: review score received by a creative work or other entity
Examples: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial <review score> 4/4

Title: nominated for
Description: award nomination received by a person, organisation or creative work (inspired from "award received" (Property:P166))
Examples: 12 Angry Men <nominated for> Academy Award for Best Picture

Title: intended public
Description: target audience: this work, product, object or event is intended for, or has been designed to that person or group of people, animals, plants, etc
Examples: Naive Set Theory <intended public> teenager

Title: MPA film rating
Description: MPA classification category: US film classification administered by the Motion Picture Association of America
Examples: Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope <MPA film rating> PG

Title: FSK film rating
Description: FSK rating category: permitted audience of a film, according to the German film-rating system (add Prüfnummer with qualifier "P2676")
Examples: Reservoir Dogs <FSK film rating> FSK 18

Title: NMHH film rating
Description: NMHH classification: rating of a film in the Hungarian film rating system
Examples: The Man from U.N.C.L.E. <NMHH film rating> Category III

Title: CNC film rating (France)
Description: CNC film classification category: category assigned to a film by the Board of Film Classification (CNC) which what audiences may view it in France
Examples: Fight Club <CNC film rating (France)> no minors under sixteen

Title: Filmiroda rating
Description: Filmiroda rating system: rating of a film in the former (2004–2011) Hungarian film rating system
Examples: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy <Filmiroda rating> Category III

Title: EIRIN film rating
Description: EIRIN film rating category: category in the Japanese film rating system (add EIRIN number with qualifier P2676)
Examples: Ushimitsu no mura <EIRIN film rating> R18+

Title: RTC film rating
Description: RTC film classification system: rating of a film in the Mexican film classification system
Examples: Logan <RTC film rating> C

Title: INCAA film rating
Description: INCAA rating system: rating of a movie in the Argentinian content rating system
Examples: Nine Queens <INCAA film rating> +13

Title: JMK film rating
Description: JMK film classification system: rating of a film in the Austrian film rating system
Examples: Amour <JMK film rating> free from 12 years

Title: KMRB film rating
Description: KMRB film rating system: rating of a film in the South Korean film/video rating system
Examples: The Handmaiden <KMRB film rating> Adults only

Title: RTC film rating
Description: RTC film classification system: rating of a film in the Mexican film classification system
Examples: Logan <RTC film rating> C

Title: FPB rating
Description: FPB rating system and FPB rating category: rating of a film or video game in the South African media content rating system
Examples: The Wound <FPB rating> 16

Title: IGAC rating
Description: IGAC classification system: rating of a film or theatrical production in the Portuguese classification system
Examples: What Now? Remind Me <IGAC rating> M/12

Title: KAVI rating
Description: Kuvaohjelmien ikärajat Suomessa: rating in the Finnish film and television rating system
Examples: The Fencer <KAVI rating> 7

Title: IMDA rating
Description: IMDA classification system: rating in the Singaporean film and video game rating system
Examples: Pop Aye <IMDA rating> M18

Title: CHVRS Classification
Description: Canadian Home Video Rating System: Canadian movie classification
Examples: Gerontophilia <CHVRS Classification> 14A

Title: RCQ classification
Description: RCQ film rating system: movie classification for the Régie du Cinéma Québécois
Examples: The Good Lie <RCQ classification> 13+
